description:
## Outcome

The CLI resolves extension IDs through trusted host records and project trust, then uses the same public Jidoka host in interactive, run, and eval modes.

## Why now

The Jidoka host is complete. The CLI can now add product configuration without owning extension runtime behavior or breaking JSONL.

## Current state

The CLI has no extension configuration, identity store, or project trust record. `agent.yml` will have inert requests after the blocking story. Runtime profiles are the only host mapping. TUI and automation start Jidoka separately but can pass public host options.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jido_cli` change. The CLI owns user/project trusted configuration, canonical project identity, trust interaction, process descriptor lookup, stderr diagnostics, and mode selection. Jidoka owns resolution validation, startup, tools, policy, state, and results.

## Detailed implementation

1. Add host record and project trust loaders under a focused CLI namespace. Record extension ID, source, version, SHA-256 pin, command only for process type, requested/granted permissions, scope, enabled state, and modes.
2. Resolve user and trusted-project records with deterministic precedence and duplicate detection.
3. Key project trust by canonical root and repository identity when available. In automation, an untrusted project fails as configuration error without a prompt.
4. Verify executable hash before giving the trusted descriptor to Jidoka. Do not place the command in a portable result.
5. Use one resolver path for TUI, `run`, and `eval`. Give each matrix cell fresh extension instances and state scoped to its session.
6. Keep extension result data under registered namespaces in case results. Keep stdout under `Automation.JSONL`; route diagnostics to stderr.
7. Reject interactive-only extensions in automation before a cell starts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Known pinned records resolve in allowed modes; unknown or changed records fail closed.
- [ ] Untrusted project configuration cannot activate an extension.
- [ ] Non-interactive trust failure emits no JSONL and exits 64.
- [ ] TUI, run, and eval pass the same public host contract.
- [ ] Separate cells receive separate process/built-in state.
- [ ] Extension failure produces one valid namespaced case error and exit 1.
- [ ] No raw command, secret, or child stdout enters `jido.case-result`.

## Test plan

- Success: user-scoped built-in and trusted project-scoped process fixture in all modes.
- Invalid input: duplicate ID, unsafe record, bad hash, untrusted project, and interactive-only automation.
- Runtime failure: record disappears, process startup fails, and extension closes with error.
- Boundary and security: agent file command is rejected/inert; project path and repository identity are canonical; stdout isolation.
- Deterministic capability: inject filesystem, repository identity, trust store, hash function, registry, and fixture host.
- JSONL and exit status: success and extension error lines, stderr diagnostics, trust status 64, runtime status 1, success 0.

## Documentation

Add CLI extension configuration and project trust guides. Explain user/project scope, pin changes, permissions, interactive versus automation modes, and no arbitrary code from agent files.

## Non-goals

Do not download or update packages. Do not add a marketplace. Do not add signatures, hot reload, custom TUI views, MCP, or subagents.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.4.6` — Host trusted process extensions through the extension host
- `jido_cli-tqg.2.2` — Run automation cells through the public Jidoka sequence
- `jido_cli-tqg.3.8` — Publish requested and confirmed enforcement evidence

Features unlocked by this story:

- Selectable default coding extensions
- Process extensions in interactive and automated runs

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jido_cli` commit. Use a message such as `feat(cli): resolve trusted CLI extensions (jido_cli-tqg.4.7)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jido_cli
mix test test/jido_cli/extensions test/jido_cli/cli/runtime_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/automation_test.exs
mix quality
mix test --cover
mix docs
```
title: Resolve trusted extensions and project trust in both CLI modes
